GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: The feature exists because providers moved to time-of-day pricing and the user has no vvoc surface that reflects it. The design settled on three cooperating pieces: a pure schedule library shared by server and TUI (no OpenCode imports, injectable clock), a chat.message server hook, and an app_bottom TUI banner. chat.message was chosen over chat.params because it fires exactly once per user message before the provider request, carries the selected model (input.model and UserMessage.model), and already has two in-repo precedents: the workflow plugin throws from it for hard stops, and system-context-injection mutates output.message.system for soft guidance. chat.params would fire per LLM step including tool loops and retries, which is noisy and late.

The hard-by-default with grace design resolves an explicit user tension: the user wanted hard blocking for everything but also wanted a session started before a window boundary to never die mid-flight. The resolution is that hard applies only to work born inside a peak window (session.time.created after window start); everything older is grandfathered to soft forever. Subagent-like agents are always soft because the admission decision happened at the parent level: if a parent tried to start during peak it was already blocked, so existing children are continuation of admitted work. This also covers guardian, which runs as a separate opencode run process without parentID but is a known subagent agent, and internal OpenCode agents (compaction, title, summary), which are infrastructure and must not be blocked or the session machinery itself breaks.

Suggestions are computed dynamically from connected providers minus peak-active ones because a static suggest list goes stale the moment a provider changes its clock or the user connects a new provider. The user explicitly rejected model-level suggestions for now: propose providers, the user picks the model. Provider-level schedule matching also survives model generation churn (deepseek V3 to V4, GLM 5.2 to 5.3, Qwen 3.7 to 3.8), which model-level tables would not.

The banner goes in app_bottom because the user explicitly rejected transient toasts for soft mode: the reminder must stay on screen and annoy. app_bottom was previously used by the branding footer before it moved to sidebar_footer, so rendering there is proven. The banner shows only when the current model's provider is in peak to keep it signal rather than noise.

Built-in schedules are materialized into vvoc.json (never overwriting user edits) following the hashline-edit routing and tool-history-compaction entry pattern, because that is how this repository keeps defaults visible, editable, and user-owned. Schedule data provenance, verified 2026-08-21: deepseek 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC daily (x2 surcharge effective 2026-08-16 per api-docs.deepseek.com; the older 16:30-00:30 UTC off-peak discount died with the V3/R1 aliases on 2026-07-24 and must not be used); z-ai 14:00-18:00 UTC+8 Mon-Fri per docs.z.ai coding plan clock (x3 vs x1 quota), which equals 06:00-10:00 UTC weekdays and forced the optional days field into the window model; qwen peak 00:00-14:00 UTC daily, derived from the 22:00-08:00 Beijing off-peak window confirmed by two independent sources (international Model Studio promo 14:00-00:00 UTC and the CN token-plan page), noting the international variant is a time-limited promotion. Defaults carry a revision date because providers move these clocks.

Auto-substitution was explicitly rejected by the user: vvoc informs, the user decides. Fail-open is the error posture because a broken schedule blocking all work would be worse than the cost it prevents; unknown providers are never blocked; and hard mode never triggers from a parsing error.

Alternatives.Alternative: Per-message grace (block only messages sent before the boundary but allow later ones based on last-activity) was rejected as unpredictable compared to session-creation-time grandfathering.
chat.params interception with an injected reminder on every step was rejected as noisy, late, and unable to cleanly block a whole run.
Auto-switching to the first off-peak suggested provider was rejected by the user as not vvoc's responsibility.
Static suggest lists in config were rejected in favor of dynamic connected-provider enumeration.
Toast-based soft warnings were rejected by the user in favor of the persistent app_bottom banner.
Model-level schedule tables were deferred: provider churn makes them fragile and current provider clocks are plan-level, not model-level.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Exact provider alias table entries (z-ai, zai, glm, qwen, alibaba id spellings seen in api.state.provider) are fixed during planning against observed provider ids.
TUI banner refresh cadence across window boundaries (event-driven re-render vs interval tick) is decided during implementation against observed slot re-render behavior.
A dedicated vvoc peak-hours CLI status command and analytics integration are candidates for a follow-up change.
Model-level or per-model windows inside one provider remain a possible future extension of the window model.

Scenarios.Scenario: Peak starts at 14:00; a session created at 13:59 keeps working with a soft note and banner only, including follow-up messages sent at 15:00; a new session created at 14:05 with the same provider is hard-blocked with suggestions of connected off-peak providers.

Five providers connected, three in peak: hard-block text and banner name only the two off-peak providers; if all connected providers are in peak, messages degrade to stating the window end and wait time without suggestions.
A workflow parent admitted before the window launches managed subagents during peak; the subagent sessions receive soft treatment only; a guardian permission review during peak is never blocked.

A user edits the deepseek window in vvoc.json; the next vvoc sync preserves the edited window and does not rewrite defaults; a malformed edited window logs a warning and disables that provider's schedule without blocking anything.
OpenCode restarts mid-peak: grace decisions are unchanged because they derive from persisted session fields, not plugin memory.
